title: Unamused Face Emoji 😒 Meaning: Side-Eye, Sulking, Shade
description: The unamused face emoji 😒 is the classic side-eye: annoyed, unimpressed, jealous or sulking. See how to tell joking from real irritation, and 😒 vs 🙄.
summary: 😒 looks away with half-closed eyes and a small frown. It means the sender is annoyed, unimpressed or sulking. It is the standard emoji for side-eye, used for irritation at a person, jealousy, disappointment and grumpy disapproval that stops short of real anger.
meaning: The face refuses to look at you, and that is the message. 😒 says “I'm not happy about this” with a turned head and a tight mouth. It follows cancelled plans, unfair decisions, bad excuses and chores assigned to the wrong person. The annoyance is real but contained. Someone who sends it is displeased enough to say so and not upset enough to argue.

Much of its use is personal. Where 😑 is tired of the situation, 😒 tends to be annoyed with someone. It is the look given to the friend who spoils an ending, the partner who liked an ex's photo, the sibling who got the bigger room. That makes it a natural fit for jealousy and feeling slighted, which is why slang like “jelly” and “salty” so often travels with it.

It is also the emoji of throwing shade. Commenting 😒 on a rival's success, a boring take or an influencer's apology video expresses disdain without wasting words. In this public use the feeling is less hurt and more contempt: the sender finds the thing beneath them and wants onlookers to know it.

Among close friends it is frequently an act. “You went to our taco place without me 😒” is pretend sulking, a way of saying “I'm jealous and I like you.” The exaggerated pout invites the other person to make it up with an apology or a joke. Telling the performance from the real thing comes down to how serious the offense was and how the rest of the chat sounds.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It registers a complaint. After “running late again,” a 😒 means the lateness has been noted. It often comes with one or two clipped words such as “wow,” “okay” or “nice.” Mock-sulking between friends looks the same but arrives with jokes around it. A 😒 followed by silence is the kind to take seriously.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Usually it is playful jealousy or a pout: you mentioned another person, took too long to answer, or made plans without them. That means they care about your attention. If it follows a comment that could have offended them, treat it as real and address it instead of teasing back.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It is a quick way to disapprove. People post it under announcements they dislike, such as price increases or a favorite show being cancelled, and under content they find smug or dull. Reaction images and “side-eye” memes cover the same ground, and 😒 is their plain-text stand-in.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Peers swap it in private messages about irritating tasks or decisions from above. In shared channels it reads as open resentment toward whoever posted. Since it tends to be about a person more than a circumstance, it is among the riskier reactions to leave on a colleague's message.

examples.text: You watched the next episode without me 😒
examples.meaning: Playfully or mildly annoyed at being left out.

examples.text: So she gets an extension and I don't 😒
examples.meaning: Resentful about treatment that seems unfair.

examples.text: Must be nice to have a beach day on a Tuesday 😒
He said he'd call and of course he didn't 😒
examples.meaning: Let down by someone, and not surprised.
Unimpressed by something seen as a marketing gimmick.

combos.meaning: Annoyed and dismissive at once; the sender has no patience left for this.
Side-eyeing a specific person, often in a group chat, to call them out jokingly.
Hurt and sulking after feeling neglected or betrayed.

confusedWith.difference: 😏 has the same sideways glance but its mouth curls up, so it reads as flirty or smug. 😒 turns the mouth down in displeasure. They are easy to mistake at a glance and mean nearly opposite things.
🙄 looks upward in exasperation or sarcasm and dismisses what was said as ridiculous. 😒 looks sideways and stays annoyed. Eye-rolling brushes something off; side-eye holds on to the grievance.
😑 is flat and worn out, a blank response to something tiresome. 😒 has more emotion in it, especially resentment or jealousy aimed at a person. 😑 has stopped caring; 😒 still does.

avoid: Do not use it in reply to someone's good news unless they will clearly take the jealousy as a joke.
Avoid leaving it as a reaction on a coworker's message in a shared channel.
Skip it when you are seriously hurt and need to be understood, because it looks like sulking and hides the real issue.
design: A yellow face with heavy, half-lowered eyelids, pupils shifted to one side, and a short mouth angled downward. Some platforms add flat or slightly furrowed brows. The designs are consistent across vendors. Its eyes are drawn almost exactly like those of the smirking face, and only the mouth separates the two.

faqs.q: What does 😒 mean from a girl or a guy?
faqs.a: They are annoyed, jealous or pretending to sulk. If it follows a mention of someone else or of plans that left them out, it is often affectionate jealousy. If you forgot something or let them down, the irritation is probably real.

Yes, it is the one most people mean. The eyes cut to the side with a frown, matching the look of silent judgment. 👀 and 🫤 are sometimes used for side-eye too, but 😒 is the one that carries disapproval.
😒 is annoyance that lingers, often at a person. 🙄 is dismissal: “that's ridiculous” or “here we go again.” Send 😒 when you are bothered and 🙄 when you think something is silly or tiresome.

Work out whether it is a joke. If the offense was trivial and the chat is light, play along or offer a mock apology. If you cancelled, forgot or said something sharp, acknowledge it directly. Ignoring a sincere 😒 usually makes it worse.

Often. It is common in replies to vacation photos, new purchases and news about an ex or a rival. The jealousy can be good-natured between friends or real in romantic situations, so consider the subject.
